To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a novel method to interpret 2D gesture drawings in 3D for augmented reality, which outperformed previous methods by better conveying the intended meaning of the user's drawing.

1) we present the first real-time method to interpret 2D gesture drawings in 3D, 2) we provide an extensive analysis of the ambiguies that arise when interpreting 2D gesture drawing and how we address them, 3) we show how to use 2D image and 3D scene cues to infer the objects of interest in the scene, and 4) our approach outperforms previous 3D gesture drawing interpretation methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of an augmented reality annotation system which can be used to enhance remote collaborative applications, and is based on a novel gesture interpretation method which can handle a wide range of 2D gesture drawings.
the problem of how to interpret 2D annotations from novel viewpoints in an AR enhanced remote collaboration scenario.
the problem of automatically interpreting 2D gestures and rendering them in a 3D environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is the first to show that it is feasible to render 2D gesture drawings from arbitrary viewpoints in 3D, and that it can do so with a high degree of accuracy.
we present an algorithm that is able to infer the meaning of a user drawing and render it in a 3D environment in a way that is consistent with the original intention of drawing it.
our approach is able to better interpret 2D gesture drawing annotations in 3d augmented reality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
by interpreting 2D gesture drawings in 3D we are able to better convey the original intention of a remote user to a local collaborator.
we provide a new approach towards interpreting 2D gesture drawings in 3D, which is a key step towards enabling more intuitive interaction with augmented reality.
our approach allows the user to draw 2D annotations and have the system interpret them as 3D gestures in augmented reality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible for a system to infer the user's intention when drawing 2D gestures, and render them in 3D to help the user better convey their ideas in augmented reality.
it is possible, and often easy to do, to interpret 2D gesture drawings in a way that is consistent with the intention of the user.
2D gesture interpretations can be enhanced by using additional information such as 3D scene geometry and user interaction.
